content.text: JobOperator is a lightweight interface used to launch, stop, restart, and monitor batch jobs programmatically.

items: Provides high-level control over job execution.
Useful for remote job management, scripting, dashboards, or CLI tools.
Can be exposed as an MBean via JMX for monitoring in tools like JConsole or VisualVM.

content.code:
<bean id="jobOperator"
      class="org.springframework.batch.core.launch.support.SimpleJobOperator">
    <property name="jobExplorer" ref="jobExplorer"/>
    <property name="jobRepository" ref="jobRepository"/>
    <property name="jobLauncher" ref="jobLauncher"/>
    <property name="jobRegistry" ref="jobRegistry"/>
</bean>

jobOperator.start("importJob", "run.id=1");
jobOperator.stop(123L); // stops execution with ID 123

content.text: JobExecutionListener allows reacting to job lifecycle events.

items: Sending notifications (email, SMS, Slack, webhook) when a job fails.

content.text: A web-based dashboard (legacy but still used in some enterprise systems) that:

items: Displays job executions, steps, parameters, exit statuses.
Allows triggering jobs from a UI.
Enables exploration of the Job Repository visually.
When visibility into job metadata is needed by QA, support, or operations teams.
When you want to start/stop jobs manually without writing code.

content.text: ⚠️ Note: Spring Batch Admin is no longer actively maintained but still appears in legacy systems. Modern alternatives include Spring Boot Actuator, Micrometer, Prometheus/Grafana, and custom dashboards.
